CVE-2026-84304 (GHSA-vp52-pcj8-j9qc, GO-2026-6348): before gRPC-Go 1.83.1, the HTTP/2 transport (internal/transport) stored each fragment of a DATA frame as a separate entry in its receive buffer, so an unauthenticated peer sending very many one-byte DATA frames over concurrent streams can exhaust process memory while staying within flow-control windows. It is fixed in google.golang.org/grpc v1.83.1, which compacts the receive buffer by default: https://github.com/grpc/grpc-go/security/advisories/GHSA-vp52-pcj8-j9qc, https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6348, https://github.com/grpc/grpc-go/pull/9331, https://github.com/grpc/grpc-go/commit/7354d9c8debb4bcf2225bf429857078de310c176, https://github.com/grpc/grpc-go/commit/8cfeca0e1ee5ea0980dcc320e20240fa1079ec77, https://github.com/grpc/grpc-go/releases/tag/v1.83.1. Read the Go build information and the function table (with a reader of the Go symbol table that also works on stripped binaries) of every build-dev package published in the DHI Alpine 3.23 repository: 90 builds, 2.6.4-r0 through the current 2.29.1-r2, each for x86_64 and aarch64 except 2.6.4-r0, which is published for aarch64 only; every download was checked against the index checksum. Version 2.19.1-r1 is listed three times in each index; the repository serves one copy, which matches one of those entries' checksum, and that copy was read. Each package holds one file, the Go program /usr/bin/build. runtime.main is in its function table in every build, so every table was read. In every build, /usr/bin/build embeds google.golang.org/grpc and links the gRPC transport functions the advisory names, including internal/transport.NewHTTP2Client, NewServerTransport and (*recvBuffer).put. Builds before 2.20.0-r12 embed google.golang.org/grpc 1.76.0, 1.79.3, 1.80.0 or 1.82.1; 2.20.0-r12 and every later build embed 1.83.1 or 1.83.2, which carry the fix.
